text:
Alyssa: Anyone seeing slow chart renders in staging after yesterday's routing-weight tweak? Dashboards with multiple small charts (sparklines/heatmaps) are janky for me.
Ben: Yep, telemetry shows main-thread parse and script-eval spikes right around the routing change window.
Mia: I pulled kvcache metrics — miss rate for the /heatmap route jumped ~3x starting at 11:10.
Sam: Could be traffic shifted to eu-canary where we still have the old splitpoint + no-prefetch config. That would cause repeated chunk rehydrates.
Ben: Network traces show repeated GETs for /static/chunks/chart-utils~worker. Looks like we're double-importing a helper in the new lazy-split.
Alyssa: Quick repro steps: open dashboard > load 8 heatmaps > observe long frame and repeated chunk loads in Network tab.
Alyssa: Minimal curl to trigger (header forces staging routing):
```
curl -H 'x-redwood-env:staging' -H 'x-region:eu' 'https://console.staging.redwood.ai/dashboards/abc?seed=8' -I
```
Mia: Confirmed — disabling eu-canary routing (switching weight back) drops chunk refetches and restores smoothness.
Ben: Proposed immediate actions: rollback routing weight to previous, hotfix to dedupe chart-utils import, and increase chunk TTL on CDN for that file. Also add a telemetry alert for chunk-load-rate and kvcache-miss spike.
Sam: For medium term we should add a client-side dedupe for worker polyfills and a canary check that verifies bundle parity across regions before shifting weight.
Alyssa: +1. Ben, can you open the PR for import dedupe and a small CDN TTL bump? I'll coordinate the rollback and a canary run after the PR merges.
Ben: Will open PR in ~15m. Also adding a quick dashboard panel under Console -> Telemetry to show chunk-loads per route.
DevEx Bot: deploy-bot: canary-rollout paused (manual) — user ben initiated a pause for investigation.
Mia: After the rollback and PR, we should run a synthetic that loads heavy dashboards from each region to verify no regression.
Sam: Agree. Also adding an annotation to the routing change so on-call can correlate future telemetry spikes to rollout events.
Alyssa: Thanks all — prioritizing this as P1 for the day since it's affecting interactive SLOs. Will post updates here. :thumbsup:
